page: Amazon Web Services r5d.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon Platinum 8259CL processor operating at 3.1 GHz across 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs with hyperthreading enabled. The system includes 512.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, providing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Attached storage consists of 2400 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 20 Gbps, and there are no included GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong memory throughput under uncached conditions, recording 209.41 GB/sec on large-block read operations and 92.36 GB/sec on large-block write tests. Multi-core performance is solid, indicated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 54,167.75 and a PassMark CPU score of 42,683.3. However, single-core benchmarks reveal architectural limitations, placing in the bottom 25% with a Geekbench single-core score of 1,057.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1,285.08. LLM text generation metrics also fall into lower percentiles due to modest per-thread throughput and the lack of specialized AI accelerators.

Cost efficiency is anchored in its dense memory footprint and high-speed local NVMe capacity. Because compute density scales across 64 vCPUs with significant memory bandwidth, workloads needing high RAM capacities achieve solid qualitative value per resource unit without the operational expense of distributed clusters. Conversely, applications constrained by single-thread latency or demanding intensive GPU execution do not leverage this instance effectively.

The r5d.16xlarge instance fits large-scale memory-resident applications, such as distributed in-memory caches, high-throughput Redis deployments, and relational database management systems. It is also suitable for data warehousing, heavy ETL processing, and scratch-space data science pipelines that benefit from direct access to 2400 GB of high-speed local NVMe storage.
description: Amazon Web Services r5d.16xlarge is a memory-optimized Nitro-based server featuring 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor at 3.1 GHz. It pairs 512.0 GB of DDR4 memory with 2400 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and a 20 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance delivers strong memory bandwidth, measuring 209.41 GB/sec on uncached reads, and reliable multi-core throughput, reflected in a PassMark CPU score of 42,683.3. Single-core performance and CPU-based LLM generation remain lower tier, making the hardware less suited for single-threaded tasks or GPU-accelerated computing. With its 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio and direct NVMe storage, r5d.16xlarge is well positioned for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, including large relational databases, in-memory caching platforms, and data warehousing pipelines requiring substantial low-latency working storage.
